data.cultural_impact: In Indian culture, Appa is used as a term of respect and love towards a father figure, carrying the deepest sense of affection and honor. In many Hindu families, the father holds an esteemed position as the primary provider, protector, and teacher.
data.spiritual_significance: Appa carries immense spiritual significance, representing the divine father figure in Hindu mythology. As per Hindu scriptures, Lord Shiva is referred to as Appa, the father of the universe, in the Ardhanarishvara form (Lord Shiva with his wife Shakti.) This name Appa signifies the creation, protection, and nurturing aspects of the divine. Honoring one's father by referring to him as Appa reaffirms the profound respect and acknowledgment of the Divine Father, and the bond between the father and child is considered a reflection of this divine connection.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The name Appa is mentioned in the Tirukkural, a 2nd-century BCE Tamil text. The name Appa carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Appa is used to refer to a father or a guardian in the Tirukkural.
